clue.text: Study of star and moon realigned to second coordinate

indicators.note: realigned says the letters of the two heavenly bodies are put into a fresh order

parts.note: in the pair (x, y) the second coordinate is y

explanation.surface: An astronomer re-plots a star and the moon on a chart's vertical axis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'realigned' scrambles STAR and MOON into ASTRONOM; then Y, the second of the x and y coordinates, ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of the heavens is a field of study.

clue.text: Prominent Socialist stranded

definitions.meaning: Peter ... was a leading Labour (socialist) cabinet minister
a stranded vessel is left on the beach, high and dry on land

explanation.surface: A leading left-winger finds himself politically marooned.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Shore was a senior Labour politician; a stranded boat lies on the beach, the land's edge.

clue.text: A bit of a pig, and more impetuous

definitions.meaning: a slice of bacon is a small portion of a pig
comparative of rash, meaning hasty or reckless

explanation.surface: Someone is being called a bit of a pig and rather reckless too.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice of bacon is part of a pig; rash means reckless, so the comparative means more reckless.

clue.text: The invader who wasn't a woman either?

definitions.text: The invader who wasn't a woman either?

parts.words: The invader who wasn't a woman either?
parts.note: a man of 1066 from northern France, and read in two words, someone who was neither a woman nor a man

explanation.surface: A riddle about the sex of a conquering soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the name into NOR and MAN: 'not a woman, nor a man', which is what 'either' points to. The invaders were the conquerors of England in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The conquerors of England in 1066 came from Normandy in northern France.

clue.text: The striker played by the football team

definitions.meaning: a safety ... is struck to light it
a game of football is a fixture the team plays

explanation.surface: A centre-forward turning out for his club.
explanation.definitionFit: A light is struck from one of these small sticks; a football fixture is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Style of architecture erected in geometrical constructions

definitions.meaning: the late English Gothic style with strong vertical lines
a line erected at a right angle to another in a geometric drawing

explanation.surface: An architectural style built up from geometric forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Late English Gothic is named for its vertical tracery; in geometry, a line set at right angles is so described.

clue.text: Putting up timber residence for putting up residents

parts.note: fixing planks in place is boarding
a house is a dwelling

explanation.surface: Building a wooden home to lodge tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting up' appears twice: first as nailing up planks, then as giving lodgers rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodging establishment gives paying guests rooms and meals.

clue.text: The devil has a way to cut food supply, and the mob protest

parts.note: a demon is a devil
St is short for street, a way
a ration is an allotted supply of food

explanation.surface: Food shortages caused by an evil figure lead the crowd to take to the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A public rally of a crowd voicing protest is a march of this kind.

clue.text: Unexpectedly simultaneously

definitions.meaning: suddenly, without warning
everything happening at the same moment

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both suddenly and at one and the same time.

clue.text: Treatise which describes a one-dimensional mathematical chart

parts.note: mono means single, one
a graph is a plotted chart in mathematics

explanation.surface: A scholarly paper explaining a simple single-axis plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly study devoted to one subject is a treatise.

clue.text: Pleas carelessly drawn up become void in time

indicators.note: a careless drafting jumbles the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Badly drafted legal pleas expire after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A right or policy that expires through time passing becomes invalid.

clue.text: Dwell tediously on a subject, and finally appeal to Marx

parts.note: to harp on is to keep returning to a topic
O is the cry of appeal, as in 'O Lord'

explanation.surface: Someone who goes on and on ends by invoking Karl Marx.
explanation.walkthrough: Marx here is not Karl but one of the Marx Brothers, the silent comedian who played the harp.
explanation.definitionFit: The silent member of the Marx Brothers comedy team went by this name.

clue.text: Honest German invader of France

definitions.meaning: candid, open
the ... were a Germanic people who conquered Gaul

explanation.surface: An honest German who invaded France.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means honest; the Germanic tribe that overran Gaul gave France its name.

clue.text: Flowers for Miss Robson

definitions.meaning: the plant life of a region
Dame ... Robson was an English actress

explanation.surface: Bouquets for an actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A region's plant life is its botanical stock; Dame Robson was a celebrated English stage and film actress.

clue.text: Assign a pound to the raffle

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)
a lot is a draw or lottery

explanation.surface: Putting a pound into the raffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion or allocate is to assign.

clue.text: The book most venerated by the King over West Algeria

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece written above another comes first

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Oran is the main city of western Algeria

explanation.surface: A sacred book revered by a monarch who rules western Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: The holy scripture of Islam is revered above all other books by Muslims.

clue.text: Garden lovers almanac?

parts.note: a yearly book, and also a plant that lives for one season, which a gardener loves

explanation.surface: A yearbook for gardening enthusiasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a yearbook, like an almanac, and a plant that completes its life in one year.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearbook appears once a year; a bedding plant that lives one season is also so called.

clue.text: Duke who was Illyrian if not Chinese

parts.note: or means otherwise, if not
Sino- is the prefix for Chinese

explanation.surface: A duke who came from Illyria, not China.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night; Illyria was a region on the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: In Twelfth Night the ruler of Illyria, who loves Olivia, is a duke.

clue.text: Tanker needed to keep the wheels of industry turning

definitions.meaning: a ship carrying oil

definitions.text: needed to keep the wheels of industry turning
definitions.meaning: something that lubricates machinery

explanation.surface: An oil ship keeping the economy running.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil-carrying ship is so called, as is a can or worker that lubricates machines.

clue.text: Bath biscuit for Cromwell

definitions.meaning: a Bath ... is a plain dry biscuit from Bath, the English spa town
... Cromwell, the English Lord Protector

explanation.surface: A biscuit from Bath named after Cromwell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bath Oliver is a cracker from the spa city of Bath; Cromwell's first name is the same.

clue.text: Malt vinegar brewed from a lager

indicators.note: brewing turns one drink into another, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Vinegar made from beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar made from sour ale is a malt vinegar.

clue.text: Where in London play has not been called off

parts.note: act means perform, play a part
an event still going ahead is on

explanation.surface: A London theatre where a show is still going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a district of west London.

clue.text: Big guns in the game of billiards

definitions.meaning: heavy artillery pieces
a shot striking two balls in succession

explanation.surface: Heavy artillery in a game of billiards.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy artillery pieces share their name with a billiards shot hitting two balls.

clue.text: The initial cost is not included by the non-clerical

parts.note: out means excluded
lay means not of the clergy

explanation.surface: Laypeople are excluded from paying the starting cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Money spent at the start of a venture is the expenditure needed to begin.

clue.text: Silly fellow who is for the chop

definitions.meaning: a fool or blockhead
the thick end of a loin of lamb or pork, cut into chops

explanation.surface: A foolish man about to be sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a dimwit; the thick end of a loin is cut into chops of that name.

clue.text: The sort of toaster needed if mum is to have breakfast in bed?

definitions.text: The sort of toaster needed if mum is to have breakfast in bed?

parts.words: The sort of toaster needed if mum is to have breakfast in bed?
parts.note: a toaster that ejects the bread, and someone has to go upstairs with the tray

explanation.surface: Choosing a toaster for Mother's Day breakfast in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The kind of toaster that ejects the slices, and also what someone must do: go briefly upstairs to mum.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster that springs the slices out is of this type.

clue.text: Dig out a story that makes the headlines

definitions.meaning: to hollow out with a ladle or shovel

definitions.text: a story that makes the headlines
definitions.meaning: an exclusive news story

explanation.surface: Unearthing a front-page story.
explanation.definitionFit: To hollow out with a ladle is to dig; an exclusive news report is also so called.

clue.text: A sweetener for the cane

parts.note: a substance that sweetens, which comes from a tall grass and gives that cane its name

explanation.surface: Something sweet to accompany a caning.
explanation.walkthrough: The cane is not punishment but the plant, a tall grass grown for its sweet sap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet crystalline substance comes from cane and beet.

clue.text: He rings an army base by dispersing oil not gas

parts.note: a camp is a military base

indicators.note: dispersing scatters the letters of the three words into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone calling an army base about spreading oil instead of gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersing' rearranges OIL NOT GAS into ANOLOGIST. 'He rings' is a bell-ringer, not a caller.
explanation.definitionFit: A student of bell-ringing is someone who rings bells.

clue.text: Use Jenny to tell the story

definitions.meaning: a spinning jenny is a machine for making thread
to narrate a tale, often a tall one

explanation.surface: Getting Jenny to narrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning jenny twists thread; to narrate a tall tale has the same idiom.
